questions.q: The elder generation often has valuable insights based on their life experiences.
questions.s:
When referring to age within a generational context, "older" is more appropriate than "elder."

    • "Elder" is typically used for individuals (e.g., my elder brother), not for groups or generations.
    • "Older generation" is the correct phrase when referring to a previous generation as a whole.

So, the corrected sentence would be: "The older generation often has valuable insights based on their life experiences."

Why "has" (Singular) and "their" (Plural) are both correct?

"The older generation" is singular:

  • The word "generation" refers to a collective group, but grammatically, it is treated as a singular noun.
  • Since "generation" is singular, we use "has" instead of "have."

"Their" is used for collective possession:

  • Even though "generation" is singular, it represents many people within that generation.
  • In modern English, "their" is often used as a gender-neutral pronoun for groups of people.

Here, "their life experiences" refers to the experiences of multiple individuals within the older generation.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the correct option.

Lots of people at the club are under 20, but there are quite _____ who aren't.
questions.s:
The correct adjective is a few.

Key Points​

  • ​​Let's look at the difference between the following adjectives:
    • few- hardly any. (used in a negative sense)
    • a few- some but not many. (used for a positive tone)
    • the few- not many but all that is available.
  • All of these adjectives are used with plural countable nouns.
  • As 'people' is a plural countable noun, 'a few' will be used in the blank part as the tone of the sentence is positive (also the adverb 'quite' isn't used with a negative adjective).
     

​Correct Sentence: Lots of people at the club are under 20, but there are quite a few who aren't.

 ​​​​Additional Information  ​​

  • ​Let's look at the difference between the following adjectives:
    • little- hardly any. (used for a negative tone)
    • a little- some but not much. (used for a positive tone)
    • the little- not much but all that is available.
  • All of these adjectives are used with uncountable nouns.

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

Her performance in the recent test was worst than her previous scores, indicating a need for additional preparation and study.
o: was worst than her previous scores
indicating a need for additional preparation and study
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'was worst than her previous scores'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
  • Here, 'was worse than her previous scores' should be used instead of 'was worst than her previous scores'.
  • "Worse" is the comparative form of the adjective "bad." It is used when comparing two things or indicating a lower degree of quality. In this context, you're comparing her recent test performance to her previous scores, and "worse" correctly conveys that it was of lower quality.
  • "Worst" is the superlative form of "bad" and is used when comparing more than two things or indicating the lowest degree of quality. Since we're comparing only two things (the recent test and her previous scores), "worse" is the appropriate choice.
  • So, the original sentence, "Her performance in the recent test was worse than her previous scores," is grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning of a lower level of performance in the recent test compared to her previous scores. 
     

Correct Sentence: Her performance in the recent test was worse than her previous scores, indicating a need for additional preparation and study.
